 The Quantum Directive: The Caretakers — Behind the Scenes  2014-06-10

Stranded at the DCA Faregate: K Street's Motorcade Meltdown, Senator Thomas's Briefing Binder, & The Telescope Emoji

June 10, 2014 — Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Dirksen Senate Office Building, & The National Mall, D.C.

Book 6, Chapter 2, Part 2: The MAR Protocol & The Telescope Protocol ↗ The Quantum Directive: The Caretakers (6 Dossiers) Copy Link: Read on Phone

Scan with your camera to continue reading this dossier on your phone or tablet.
Story Date & Time 2014-06-10 • 08:21
Setting DCA Capital Transit Mezzanine • Dirksen Senate Office Building • Building 33 Chief of Staff Desk
Archival Source K Street Government Affairs Dispatch, Senate Judiciary Staff, & Marcus Chen (Building 33)
Addressed To Deployment Postmortem — Washington, D.C. Congressional Testimony

In Book 6, Chapter 2: "The Fenwick Bridge Protocol" (June 10, 2014), CEO Cassandra Vance, LPN David Vance, Liz Carter, and Casey Vance roll off Quantum's DASSP-cleared corporate jet at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), walk straight past four idling armored Apex Mountaineers, tap four auto-reloading CapitalPass cards at the elevated Capital Transit station, ride the Yellow and Blue Lines to Capitol South right on schedule, dismantle Senator Thomas's travel-expense ambush live on the Judiciary Committee monitors, execute a seamless sixty-second 10:05 AM cold-chain biologic check at the witness table, and spend their afternoon eating cheeseburgers at Rocket Burger inside the Finch Air and Space Museum.

Left breathless behind closing glass barriers at DCA—and locked out of the master Redmond itinerary—were Quantum's high-priced K Street lobbyists and Senator Thomas's shell-shocked legislative staff. Here is what happened on their side of the glass.

1. 8:21 AM — Greg's Catastrophic Pivot Back to the I-395 Parking Lot

When the glass Capital Transit faregates chimed harsh red and clamped shut on senior K Street lobbyist Greg's tailored suit waist at 8:21 AM, Cassandra had actually handed him the winning rescue instruction before boarding the platform elevator: turn around to the kiosk, buy a five-dollar Single Ride card, catch the next Yellow Line train across the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge six minutes behind us, and arrive on Capitol Hill with forty minutes to spare.

Instead, humiliated in front of two commuters after tapping his gold corporate credit card futilely against an optical transit sensor—and panicked when the ticket vending machine rejected his crumpled fifty-dollar bill—Greg made the worst tactical decision of his lobbying career.

At 8:25 AM, as the next northbound Yellow Line train glided smoothly onto the aerial track thirty feet above his head, Greg abandoned the kiosk and sprinted back across the pedestrian skybridge to his four idling Apex Mountaineers.

"Go! Go! Hit the sirens— wait, we aren't federal police, just merge onto the Parkway NOW!" Greg barked, diving into the passenger seat of Vehicle 1 while wiping sweat off his forehead with a silk pocket square.

Within four hundred yards of exiting the airport loop, Cassandra's 8:15 AM traffic math came true to the letter:

  • 8:34 AM (I-395 Northbound Merge): A stalled gravel truck near the Glebe Road interchange backed all four regular lanes of the Shirley Highway into bumper-to-bumper concrete stasis, trapping the four three-ton black SUVs behind two commuter buses and a moving van.
  • 8:38 AM (Overhead on the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge): Less than a quarter mile downstream across the Potomac shimmer, a silver six-car Capital Transit Yellow Line train—carrying the Chief Executive Officer of a trillion-dollar corporation, her nurse brother, her sister, and her sister-in-law—glided unobstructed across the river span at fifty miles per hour and plunged cleanly into L'Enfant Plaza.
  • 9:30 AM (14th Street Bridge Center Span): At the exact minute Chairman Hayes gaveled the Senate Judiciary Committee to order—and reporters photographed four starkly empty leather chairs in Quantum's reserved front-row handler gallery—Greg kicked open the heavy armored door of Vehicle 1 in dead-stopped bridge traffic and began jogging one point four miles uphill in Italian leather dress shoes through 84°F Potomac humidity, arriving outside the empty hearing room ninety seconds after Senator Patty Morrison had escorted the Vance pack down to the private Capitol Subway.

2. Inside Senator Thomas's Briefing Binder: How the Willard Ambush Backfired (9:48 AM)

Behind the raised mahogany dais of the Judiciary Committee room, Senator Thomas's Communications Director had spent Monday night highlighted-tabbing an anonymous tip planted in the tech gossip blog Silicon Valley Unfiltered: an airport tail-number spotter had logged Quantum's Laurentian corporate jet filing a DASSP slot into DCA with four Vance family members aboard, paired with a suite reservation under the Vance name at the historic Willard on Pennsylvania Avenue.

Convinced that the famously frugal "bus-riding Courtyard CEO" had secretly hypocritically billed shareholders tens of thousands of dollars for a family D.C. vacation, Thomas's staff pre-wrote a blistering press release scheduled to auto-send to forty Capitol Hill reporters at 10:00 AM.

At 9:51 AM, when David Vance tapped his clinical tablet to mirror Cassandra's brushed-aluminum MagnaByte mPad onto the committee's overhead 4K monitors—displaying Quantum Treasury's audited receipt showing Cassandra had personally written private checks reimbursing 100% of the single shared Willard pull-out-sofa suite and four commercial first-class equivalent airfares ($0.00 shareholder cost), immediately followed by Senator Thomas's own public FY2013 FEC disclosures showing $142,000 in PAC- and taxpayer-subsidized St. Thomas resort junkets—Thomas's Communications Director lunged across the back staff bench and frantically deleted the scheduled 10:00 AM press blast forty seconds before dispatch.

Fourteen minutes later, after David quietly unzipped his insulated cold-chain pouch at 10:05 AM, checked Cassandra's wrist sphygmomanometer (112/72), administered her scheduled five-second subcutaneous biologic peptide into her left upper arm while she dissected federal server encryption without dropping a syllable, and logged the entry cleanly into his MAR, Chairman Hayes leaned toward Senator Patty Morrison in the private corridor behind the dais upon adjournment.

"Thirty years I've chaired oversight panels in this building, Patty," Hayes remarked quietly, tucking his reading glasses into his breast pocket. "Most witnesses bring six $1,200-an-hour K Street handlers to whisper excuses in their ears and dodge five-word questions. That woman rode the Yellow Line in from National with her family, brought her own receipts on a tablet, didn't flinch during a cold-chain injection mid-sentence, and didn't bill her shareholders a nickel. Tell your folks back in Puget Sound I'll vote to fund her Redmond transit bridge tomorrow."

3. Chief of Staff Marcus Chen's Coffee Mug in Building 33 (1:15 PM – 2:32 PM EDT)

Back in Redmond—where it was 10:15 AM PDT inside Building 33—Chief of Staff Marcus Chen sat calmly reviewing Q3 cloud capacity tables with a mug of medium-roast coffee beside his monitor while the Vance deployment - d.c. group thread with K Street lobbyist Greg and Manhattan PR director Pierce lit up on his secondary display.

Unlike external retainers hired to manage traditional Fortune 50 egos, Marcus held Read Access to Cassandra's true master schedule—including the sacred blacked-out blocks marked simply PACK PERIMETER — NON-NEGOTIABLE:

Building 33 Chief of Staff Master Itinerary — Tuesday, June 10, 2014 (EDT)
• 08:15 – 09:15 — DCA Tarmac -> Capital Transit Yellow/Blue Line -> Capitol South (Zero Motorcade)
• 09:30 – 11:15 — U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee Testimony + LPN 10:05 Cold-Chain MAR Window
• 11:30 – 12:45 — Civilian Reset & Lunch w/ David, Liz, & Casey (Finch Air and Space Museum — Rocket Burger)
• 13:00 – 14:30 — Large-Format Space Documentary (HARD CELLULAR POWER-OFF — DO NOT ESCALATE)
• 14:30 – 16:45 — Orbital & Apollo Exhibition Wing Tour (Lead Guide: David Vance)
• 17:00 — L'Enfant Plaza Blue Line -> Farragut West -> Hotel Check-In

When Pierce threatened at 2:05 PM EDT (11:05 AM PDT) to alert Capitol Police because Cassandra's cellular ping had gone dark along Independence Avenue for sixty-five minutes, Marcus typed two calm lines—"Stand down, both of you. She is in a movie theater." and "She promised her brother a trip to the Finch. Do not call the police, Greg. Just wait for the documentary to end."—and went back to his spreadsheet.

Nineteen minutes later, at 2:31 PM EDT, Cassandra booted her phone outside the Apollo command module exhibit, read forty-seven hyperventilating handler texts, replied with a single 🔭 emoji, and muted the thread. Three thousand miles away in Building 33, Marcus Chen laughed out loud, took a sip of coffee, and archived the deployment as 100% Nominal.
